learning_outcomes.text: The course aims to provide students with knowledge of: i) the theory of DC and AC steady-state electrical circuits, and first-order transients, ii) electromagnetism and its applications in electrical engineering, iii) the basic principles of electrical safety.
The student must be able to apply the acquired knowledge to solve problems of electrical circuit analysis in steady-state and alternating current regimes.
The student must be able to identify solutions to fundamental problems in electrical engineering, including in the field of safety.
Ability to choose the most appropriate method for solving proposed electrical circuits, based on the problem-solving tools acquired during the course.
Ability to use correct technical-scientific language.
Ability to learn the theoretical and practical aspects of electrical engineering, also using teaching materials or personal research on course topics and related topics.

syllabus_topics: Fundamental concepts: charge and current, voltage, power and energy
Two-port networks, generators, resistors, capacitors and inductors, constitutive relations, Ohm's law
Elements of network topology, Kirchhoff's current and voltage laws
Two-port networks in series, parallel, star and delta connections
Ohm's law in AC, impedance, phase shift
Star or delta connection, phase and line quantities
Power in symmetric and balanced three-phase systems
Magnetic circuits and basics of electrical machines
Hazard limits of current and voltage
Protection against direct and indirect contacts
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an optional oral interview. The written test involves solving two exercises related to electrical circuits in steady-state and alternating current regimes within one and a half hours, plus theoretical questions in an additional 30 minutes (or an optional oral interview). The minimum passing grade is 18/30. Students achieving 30/30 with excellent application skills in the oral exam will be awarded 'cum laude'.
bibliography: C. Alexander, M. Sadiku, “Circuiti Elettrici” - McGraw-Hill.
